decisive_correction.false_universal_claim: Every point of a moving open half lies in one fixed reference OPEN half.
decisive_correction.reason: When the moving cut differs from the reference cut, a point on the old reference cut circle can be an interior point of the moving half.
decisive_correction.correct_split: First prove membership in the full original negative component. Then split the physical radius into < reference cut, > reference cut, or = reference cut. The first two yield a genuine fixed reference unitStrip point; the equality case is a closure/continuity argument at an interior component point.
decisive_correction.consequence: Dropping the equality branch would lose points quantified by CanonicalPrimitiveGeometry.materialJets.

actual_scalar.exact_definition: atom D T S C L V z ℓ chartRadial q = ((V.chart z ℓ (physicalUnitPoint V ℓ q)).1 - V.left ℓ) / (V.right ℓ - V.left ℓ).

actual_scalar.why_not_inverseRadial: inverseRadial samples a canonical point and normalizes its image by physical length. It is not the normalized forward coordinate needed to certify the opposite-root u range at a prescribed moving physical point.

single_shrink.zeroth_bound: Choose loss₀ from hcur.2.1 once, then choose B₀>0 from its s=0 clause. For all ℓ and q∈unitStrip: |F| ≤ B₀ E0(sample(V.cell ℓ))^B₀ H(sample(V.cell ℓ))^(3/4) parameterGrading S loss₀ ζ.

single_shrink.choice: δ=1/4; M=B₀*CH; base'=max base loss₀; ε'=min ε (δ/(2*M)). First align any finitely many existing bases/radii by max/min and restriction if they are not already identical.
single_shrink.proof: parameterGrading loss₀ ζ = sectorGrading loss₀ ζ.1 + |ζ.2| < 2 ε'. Hence |F| < M*2ε' ≤ δ.
single_shrink.quantifiers: loss₀,B₀,CH and the single base'/ε' are chosen before every component, side, point, derivative order N and later parameter-jet order. No later order-dependent neighborhood shrink is needed for this range step.

range_argument.same_reference_side: If the reference side t equals current target s, the required target forward/height/Jacobian fields are sampled directly at a valid fixed reference unit point. No opposite-root conversion is needed.
range_argument.crossed_reference_side: If t=!s, use the genuine fixed reference opposite-half unit point q, and set u=(K.chart z k_(!s) x).1/ρ_m and v=(K.chart z k_s x).1/ρ_m.
range_argument.upper: The true reference chart maps its reference half to (0,ρ_m), hence u_ref∈(0,1). The chartRadial difference bound gives u<u_ref+1/4<5/4. At the reference cut the continuity argument gives u≤5/4.
range_argument.lower: Current target MapsTo gives 0<v<1. n04bActualTypedAtlas_negative_opposite_normalized at x∈Ω_m gives u>0 and v^(3/2)+u^(3/2)=2. Since v^(3/2)<1, u^(3/2)>1 and u>1.
range_argument.output: Thus crossed points have 1<u<5/4 off the old cut and 1<u≤5/4 on it. A common [1,5/4] range is valid for all crossed points.
actual_suppliers: CanonicalGeometry.charts at z and at ref, with CanonicalGeometry.referenceDomain at ref
range_argument.angular_identity: Both actual root charts have the same travel angle at the same physical point; retain this literal equality. Do not replace that travel angle by the physical angle or reference angle.

normalized_conversion.first_differential: The first differential row changes by -sqrt(u/g(u)); the second (angular) row is unchanged.
normalized_conversion.fixed_compact_cost: On [1,5/4], u^(3/2)≤u²≤25/16, hence 2-u^(3/2)≥7/16. Set c=(7/16)^(2/3)>0. Then c≤g(u)≤1, (4c/5)^(1/4)≤height factor≤1, and 1≤Jacobian factor≤sqrt(5/(4c)).
normalized_conversion.derivative_cost_scope: The normalized scalar conversion functions and their reciprocals are smooth on a neighborhood of this fixed compact interval. Their finite-order constants depend on the order, not m, travel, the raw optical lower bound or a new collar width. Raw chart reconstruction still multiplies by the actual ρ_m, and physical/unit derivative conversion still pays the true widths.
normalized_conversion.not_formalized_here: The compact scalar inequalities and the final domain gluing are mathematical deductions recorded here; no new Lean theorem was written or claimed compiled.
